subsections.title: Overview
subsections.summary: What it is and why it matters.

blocks.html: Your browser is the window you use to see almost everything online — and the window works both ways. Websites, advertisers and trackers can read a lot about you through it: what you visit, what you click, and enough details about your device to recognise you again later. Choosing a private browser and setting it up well removes most of that tracking without changing how you use the web.

blocks.label: Incognito isn’t privacy
blocks.html: Private or incognito mode only stops your browser from keeping a history on your device. The websites you visit, advertisers, your internet provider and Google can all still see what you do. Real privacy tools change what those parties can collect in the first place.

subsections.title: Terminology
subsections.summary: The words you will run into.

items.title: Tracker
items.html: A script or pixel from a third party (often an ad company) that follows you from site to site.

items.title: Cookie
items.html: A small file a site stores in your browser. Useful for logins, but third-party cookies are used for tracking.

items.title: Fingerprinting
items.html: Identifying your browser from its unique mix of settings, fonts, screen size and hardware, without cookies.

items.title: Extension
items.html: An add-on that changes what your browser does, like an ad blocker. Each one can also see your browsing.

items.title: Global Privacy Control (GPC)
items.html: A signal your browser sends telling sites not to sell or share your data.

items.title: Chromium / Gecko
items.html: The two main browser engines. Chrome, Brave and Edge use Chromium; Firefox and LibreWolf use Gecko.

blocks.html: Judged on usability, privacy, customizability, philosophy, respect for the user, looks, and resource usage.

items.label: Brave
items.desc: Blocks ads, trackers and fingerprinting the moment you install it, no setup needed. It runs Chrome extensions, which makes it the easiest switch if you're coming from Chrome. You can switch off the extras you don't need (crypto wallet, Rewards, the Leo AI assistant) in settings.

items.label: DuckDuckGo
items.desc: Blocks trackers and tells sites not to sell your data (Global Privacy Control) by default. The Fire button wipes your tabs and browsing data in one tap. The simplest option here, but it has no extensions on desktop and only limited ad blocking. Its AI features can be turned off in settings.

items.label: Mullvad Browser
items.desc: Built with the Tor Project. It has Tor Browser's anti-fingerprinting, so every user looks the same to websites, but it skips the slow Tor network. Ads and trackers are blocked by default. It doesn't hide your IP on its own, so pair it with a VPN.

items.label: Safari
items.desc: Apple's built-in browser. It limits cross-site tracking and fingerprinting automatically. On iPhone every browser uses Safari's engine anyway, which is why Privacy Guides recommends it for iOS. Add uBlock Origin Lite (available since 2025) to block ads.

items.label: Firefox
items.desc: The main independent alternative to Chrome, with the widest range of privacy extensions. Out of the box, though, it sends usage data to Mozilla and has AI features switched on. Change a few settings to make it private; our hardening guide walks you through it. Hardening guide →

items.label: LibreWolf
items.desc: Firefox with the privacy work already done: Mozilla's telemetry removed, strict tracking protection on, and uBlock Origin pre-installed. You keep Firefox's flexibility and extensions without configuring anything yourself.

items.label: Tor Browser
items.desc: Routes your traffic through three volunteer-run relays, so the sites you visit never see your real IP or location. It offers the strongest anonymity available, but pages load slower and some sites block it. Use it when anonymity matters, not for everyday browsing.

blocks.html: How each browser stacks up on the privacy features that matter most, out of the box. Select a column to download that browser.

blocks.note: Brave hides your IP only in its Tor windows (desktop); Safari only with a paid iCloud+ subscription (Private Relay).

subsections.title: Safer Browsing Habits
subsections.summary: Settings and habits for any browser.

items.details: Most updates fix security holes. Firefox and Chrome update themselves, but check now and then; Tor Browser updates separately.
One hardened browser for sensitive things (banking, health, activism), another for everyday browsing.

items.text: Set a private default search engine
items.details: DuckDuckGo, Brave Search, Mojeek or Startpage. See search engines.

items.text: Type addresses instead of searching for them
items.details: Searching a bank’s name can surface lookalike scam sites. Turn off search suggestions in the address bar.
Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → HTTPS-Only Mode. Chrome: “Always use secure connections”.
Firefox: Enhanced Tracking Protection on Strict (drop to Standard if sites break). Chrome: block third-party cookies and use Enhanced Safe Browsing.

items.text: Review camera, microphone and location permissions
items.details: Only allow them for sites you trust, and remove old permissions.

items.text: Don’t save passwords in the browser
items.details: Use a password manager instead, and delete the logins your browser saved.
Install only from the official add-on stores and remove anything you don’t use or recognise — every extension can see your browsing.
Set the browser to clear cookies and site data when it closes, and don’t reopen the last session on startup.
They can send the page you’re reading to the browser maker. Firefox: Settings → AI Controls. Chrome: turn off Gemini features.
If the browser warns a site is dangerous, don’t continue. Pause before opening links sent by message or email.

subsections.title: More Private Browsers
subsections.summary: Top picks for desktop and phone.

items.label: LibreWolf
items.desc: Hardened Firefox with tracking and fingerprinting protection built in.

items.label: Brave
items.desc: Blocks ads and trackers by default; easiest switch from Chrome.

items.label: Helium
items.desc: Chromium-based, with uBlock Origin and tracker blocking on by default.

items.label: Firefox
items.desc: Mozilla’s independent browser; harden it with a few settings.

items.label: Firefox Focus
items.desc: Mobile browser that blocks trackers and forgets everything when closed.

items.label: DuckDuckGo
items.desc: Simple browser that blocks trackers, with a one-tap Fire button.

items.label: Brave
items.desc: Blocks ads and trackers by default.

items.label: Firefox
items.desc: Supports full extensions like uBlock Origin on Android.

items.label: Firefox Focus
items.desc: Private-by-default, forgets everything on close.

items.label: DuckDuckGo
items.desc: Tracker blocking and a one-tap Fire button.

items.label: IronFox
items.desc: Hardened Firefox fork for Android with telemetry removed.

items.label: Cromite
items.desc: Open-source Chromium fork with ad blocking and anti-fingerprinting.

blocks.html: On iPhone every browser uses Safari’s engine, so pick by features: Brave, DuckDuckGo, Firefox Focus or Safari with an ad blocker.

items.label: uBlock Origin
items.desc: The essential ad and tracker blocker. Full version works in Firefox.

items.label: uBlock Origin Lite
items.desc: The version for Chrome, Edge, Brave and Safari.

items.label: ClearURLs
items.desc: Strips tracking codes out of the links you click.

items.label: Decentraleyes
items.desc: Serves common web libraries locally so third parties don’t see the request.

items.label: Cookie AutoDelete
items.desc: Deletes a site’s cookies when you close its tab.

items.label: SponsorBlock
items.desc: Skips sponsor segments in YouTube videos.

items.label: Privacy Badger
items.desc: EFF’s tracker blocker that learns as you browse.

items.label: NoScript
items.desc: Blocks scripts on sites you don’t trust. Advanced — breaks many sites.

blocks.before: Start with an ad blocker — uBlock Origin on Firefox, uBlock Origin Lite on Chrome-based browsers and Safari. Add others only if you need them. See Browser Extensions for setup.

blocks.html: Safari: uBlock Origin Lite and SponsorBlock are available from the App Store; AdGuard (a sponsored pick on privacytools.io) is another option.
